decisions.reason: Address autocomplete builds on the firm's core address and grid-area database, so it costs little to run, supports data quality for customer processes, and fits the planned move toward more SaaS.

The Austrian gas grid fee database extends the firm's established fee-database expertise into a neighbouring regulated market; it carries some risk of limited demand but is cheap to maintain alongside existing data operations.
Peak load window determination is a regulated network-operator obligation that recurs every year, which makes this a sticky, compliance-driven service close to the core business.
End-customer tariff data is valuable market data for suppliers and comparison uses, and it complements the firm's fee databases and analytics.
Custom web services rest on the existing infrastructure, are flexible project business, and align with the platform and integration strategy.
Postal code lookup is a low-cost spin-off of the established geographic and grid-area data that supports other services, although it could later be merged into the address service.
